reported.title: E-stop polarity inverted: contactor drops when e-stop is released
reported.description: estopActive() at line 20 returns true when the pin reads HIGH, but the e-stop is active LOW (pressed pulls D3 to GND), so the logic is inverted. With D3 HIGH (released) the firmware treats it as stopped and drives D5 LOW at line 74, and with D3 LOW (pressed) it falls through to setContactor(true) at lines 78/82. Measured evidence confirms this: D5 was not HIGH for 700 ms while D3 was HIGH, and not LOW for 48 ms while D3 was LOW. D5 was in the wrong state for 4842 ms across 31 interval(s), first at 100 ms: D5 was not HIGH for 700 ms while required (grace 100 ms).

exposing_checks.behaviour: D5 must follow its stimulus; HIGH when D3 == 1; LOW when D3 == 0; within 100 ms (Contactor follows e-stop)

judge_input.spec:
- E-stop on D3 with INPUT_PULLUP, active LOW when pressed. Contactor coil on D5. Run request on D6 (pull-up).
- Contactor D5 must drop LOW when e-stop is held (D3 LOW), and run HIGH when e-stop is released.
- React within 100 ms of a settled e-stop level change.
- Settle the e-stop contact for 30 ms before counting a new trip.
- Print `hoist run=<0|1> trips=<n>` every 1100 ms.
- When e-stop is clear, keep the contactor available (HIGH) for hoist motion.
